extra.message: The Flask session secret key is hardcoded ('Harry Potter And The Deathly Hallows'). Because Flask signs the session cookie with this key, anyone who knows it (it is committed to source) can forge session cookies and set 'logged_in': True to bypass authentication.

User-supplied input from request.form['expression'] is passed directly to eval(). This allows arbitrary Python code execution, e.g. submitting __import__('os').system('...') leads to full remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code (Eval Injection)

extra.message: User input from request.form['address'] is concatenated into a shell command string ('nslookup ' + address) and executed via os.popen. An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. '; cat /etc/passwd') to execute arbitrary OS commands.

The lxml XMLParser is configured with no_network=False and DTD validation enabled, then parses untrusted XML from request.form['xml']. This allows XML External Entity (XXE) attacks enabling local file disclosure (e.g. via SYSTEM 'file:///etc/passwd' entities) and SSRF through external DTD/entity resolution.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User input from request.form['name'] is interpolated into a template string that is then passed to render_template_string(). This results in Server-Side Template Injection (Jinja2), e.g. submitting {{7*7}} or {{config}} / {{ ''.__class__.__mro__... }} payloads leads to data exposure and remote code execution.

The result derived from request.form['expression'] is concatenated directly into an HTML response string returned to the browser without escaping. Attacker-controlled content is reflected unescaped, enabling reflected Cross-Site Scripting.
Output containing user-controlled request.form['address'] is concatenated directly into the HTML response without escaping, allowing reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

User input request.form['name'] is embedded unescaped into HTML ('
Hello %s!...') and rendered, enabling reflected Cross-Site Scripting in addition to the SSTI issue.

Flask is run with app.debug = True. The Werkzeug interactive debugger exposes stack traces and an interactive console (PIN-protected but bypassable) that allows arbitrary code execution, and leaks sensitive application/source information.

User passwords from request.form['password'] are stored directly in the database without hashing (see User model password column and registration). Credentials are kept in cleartext, exposing all user passwords on a database compromise.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: The /dashboard route and the sensitive functionality routes /evaluate, /lookup, /xml and /sayhi perform no session/authentication check (no session.get('logged_in')). Any unauthenticated user can access these privileged features, constituting missing authorization / broken access control.

State-changing POST endpoints (e.g. /register, /login) have no CSRF token validation and no CSRF protection (Flask-WTF / CSRFProtect) is configured. This allows Cross-Site Request Forgery against authenticated users.
